title: Credits · Catnet Systems
text: Credits a production kittyn Creator & Creative Director Game design, world direction, and production of SpookCo: Last Stop — a cooperative horror world for VRChat. Platform & development tools Platform: VRChat SDK and UdonSharp. Development tools: Blender, Clip Studio Paint, Affinity, and Codex. In-world fonts: Noto Sans JP from the Noto CJK project supports English and Japanese UI under the SIL Open Font License; its license ships with the world. Liberation Sans, supplied through TextMesh Pro, is also credited in the world's Credits page with its complete font license. The website uses system fonts. Its night-shift illustration is original SVG artwork, not a gameplay screenshot. Shader acknowledgments VRChat and Xiexe: Toon shading uses VRChat's Mobile/Toon Lit, based in part on XSToon by Xiexe, with additional modifications for SpookCo. Unity Technologies: Additional shader components are based on Unity's built-in shaders. David Hoskins and David A. Roberts: The Depot Surface grain helper uses Hash without Sine, with an HLSL adaptation based on Roberts's MIT-licensed publication. Read the complete shader copyright and license notices . Inspiration SpookCo draws on short-round horror and scavenging games. No characters, models, audio, or code from Terrors of Nowhere or SlashCo are included. Ready to clock in? Start with the player guide or return to SpookCo: Last Stop .

title: Controls & accessibility
text: Controls & accessibility Use the Controls & Accessibility panel beside dispatch’s ready board. You can also reach it from the van and personal inventory. Preferences are saved separately for desktop, VR, and touch. Choose your language On a first visit, the game waits for your saved profile, then shows a bilingual English/Japanese picker if no supported language is saved. On desktop, press 1 for English or 2 for Japanese in that initial picker, or hold Tab and click. In VR, use the personal-menu pointer on the floating picker. Change it later under Controls → i18n / Language . The choice is saved across visits and shared between your desktop and VR profiles; resetting controls does not reset language. It changes only your own view, so the crew can use different languages. Website language links do not change your in-world setting. Branding, legal notices, and developer diagnostics retain their original text. Desktop: keep chase actions on keys Action Default Temporary cursor menu Hold Tab ; release to close the entire menu Keep menu open for reading I ; press again to close Draw reusable equipment 1 Draw equipped consumable 2 Stow personal item 3 Select reserve 1 / 2 4 / 5 Drop task cargo 6 Use drawn item Native Use action / Use button Collect or work Targeted world interaction / context action On the tested desktop client, Tab stops movement. This also happened in another world. Plan cursor interaction while stationary, preferably in the refuge. Shift+Tab may not open the menu while sprinting; release sprint first. I keeps a reading panel visible but does not unlock the mouse: hold Tab to click. The six numbered shortcuts work without Tab, including with Shift held. They can be rebound, and conflicting bindings are reported. Reserve selection swaps the chosen reserve into the equipped slot; it does not draw or consume it. Press 2 to draw, then make a fresh Use input. A saved Tab Hold / Stay open preference is available. VR: wrist or floating panel Flick the right stick up or down to put the next item in your hand: hands free, your gear, then each consumable you carry. Pull the trigger on that hand to use it. Nothing needs confirming and no menu needs opening. At dispatch, hold the stick up for about half a second to ready up or unready, and hold it down to open the menu; the ready post on the floor by the ramp does the same by touch. Choose either wrist and either equipment hand. Holding the stick down is how the menu opens; there is no button on the wrist, and opening the menu does not freeze movement. Wrist mode keeps the panel attached to your chosen wrist, so it travels with your arm. Floating mode places the panel once, level in front of you, at the moment you open it; switching tabs never moves it again. Height, distance and size are adjustable for seated play and different avatar scales. The floating panel closes itself when you move more than three metres from where it was placed, when the expedition starts, when you pick up cargo, and when you take a hit or go down. If it ends up out of reach, the launcher — which sits below your wrist while the panel is open, clear of the Close corner — closes it, and pressing again places a fresh panel in front of you. Recenter in settings does the same. Menus cannot be opened during transit between stops. Buttons that duplicate VRChat's own controls are hidden unless the current situation needs them, so the panel stays compact. Your wrist carries one thing: a readout card that shows whenever you look toward that hand within arm's reach: the round, your cash, health and level, anything acting on you (soda, Adrenaline, slowed, fog, EMF bearing) and what is in your hand. Alerts stay visible whether or not the panel is open. Wrist HUD +/- on the Controls tab (office board or menu) sets the card's size, saved with your profile. Personal items follow the chosen hand. Cargo uses normal pickup controls, or the accessible Carry / Drop actions. If a native pickup occupies the equipment hand, stow or move it deliberately; personal equipment must not forcibly release it. Phone and tablet Use the screen’s MENU , USE ITEM , and COLLECT / WORK buttons. The world-space lobby boards are also present, but the screen controls are the intended touch shortcut. Inside inventory, select equipment, consumables, or reserves; use the separate Use action to activate the selected item. The iPhone build has been tried by the creator. Final touch layout and ergonomics still need broader device testing. Preferences and practice Hold or toggle repair/rescue interactions. Accessible cargo carrying with the same reservation, penalty, delivery, and drop rules. Wrist/equipment handedness, floating panel placement/size, and the wrist HUD size. Desktop key rebinding with conflict feedback and reset defaults. Separate persisted control profiles for each input family. Stick item select, on by default in VR: neutral deadzone 0.25, activation threshold 0.70, dwell 150 ms. Return to neutral before another step; each step equips outright. These settings control SpookCo actions, not VRChat’s native movement bindings. The free practice bay is closed during live playtesting; its console and supplies are hidden and answer with a notice if reached. Selecting or collecting an item never activates it automatically. The lobby's two big boards stand in the dispatch office, front right of spawn.

title: Equipment & field supplies
text: Equipment & field supplies Your inventory You have one reusable equipment slot , one equipped consumable , two reserve consumables , and one separate task-cargo slot . Duplicates are allowed; each occupies a slot. Purchases and scavenged supplies use the same three-slot pouch. Only one personal item is actively held at a time. Switching personal items does not discard cargo. Selecting a reserve swaps it with the equipped consumable. Collecting, selecting, and drawing do not automatically use an item; consuming one does not activate the next. On desktop, carried cargo and fuel use small HUD indicators, and the selected personal item appears as an icon with its name. These replace the obstructing first-person held models. Dropping cargo, docking fuel, using a consumable, or stowing an item clears the corresponding indicator. VR keeps normal hand models, and carried objectives remain visible to other players. Reusable equipment Unlocks require both a banked XP level and a lifetime commendation milestone. Commendations are not spent. Later equipment is deliberately a longer-term goal. Equipment Level Commendations Role Wind-up decoy 1 0 Place a distraction to pull the hunter’s investigation away. Instant camera 4 12 A close-range flash can stun the killer; cooldowns and post-stun immunity limit repeated use. EMF pager 12 120 Passive proximity information about the killer. Trip alarm 18 400 Place one temporary alarm. A nearby killer triggers a positional signal and a brief stun; committed charges continue through it. Track shoes 24 1,200 Passive 10% movement bonus, within the shared bonus cap. Pager and shoes work without an active Use effect. Gear selection happens during shopping/loadout windows. Active gear has cooldowns; reconnecting or resetting must not refresh them. Cash consumables These prices and effects describe the current baseline and may be rebalanced. Supply Cash Effect Field ration 18 Restores one health when below your maximum. Sprint soda 16 Eight-second movement boost; total positive movement bonuses cap at 20%. Rescue flare 22 Rescues a nearby downed teammate within 12 metres. Needs a valid teammate. Repair tape 20 Fixes one incomplete generator task step. You still press Start Engine yourself. Smoke canister 24 Ten seconds of visual concealment. Blocks killer sight through its cloud, but not hearing or attacks already in motion. Scrap bolt bundle 12 Toss a distraction onto nearby ground. Shares the decoy's resistance window; committed attacks ignore it. Door brace 18 Brace a nearby closed door for up to 45 seconds. Adds four seconds to one normal breach; charges break through. Opening the door removes it. Tool oil 20 Use beside an unfinished fueled generator for 25 seconds of easier startup controls and half the work-noise range. Flash bulb 24 One aimed camera-strength flash. Shares stun resistance with the camera and trip alarm. Emergency battery 28 Recharges your equipped active gear. Requires an active cooldown; an already armed trip alarm prevents recharging that alarm. The shop has three supply pages. Perks and consumables can complement each other: oil provides the same control assistance as Mechanic and combines with Silent Tools for quieter work, while a flash bulb provides a one-use alternative when your reusable slot holds something else. Smoke does not make you bulletproof or silence your movement. If the effect has no valid target, the request is rejected without spending the item. The shop guarantees a chosen supply, while field scavenging trades time and risk for a shared find. A repaired generator recharges active gear twice as fast within six metres , during work and extraction. Solid walls block its power, and multiple generators do not stack. A normal 30-second cooldown takes about 15 seconds if you stay connected; Quickdraw reduces that to about 12. The HUD and wrist show GENERATOR: GEAR RECHARGE 2x while connected. EMF and track shoes are passive, so they do not recharge. Power does not protect you from killers or extend extraction. Selling Use Sell equipped consumable on the Shop page to sell the supply in your equipped slot. Selling is available in the same windows as buying, not in the field. Select it again within four seconds (or hold the button) to confirm. Bought supplies refund half their price; supplies found in the field refund a quarter and are marked (found) in your inventory. The practice bay is closed in this build, so its discard action is unavailable. Shared field loot Each stop rolls supplies at distinct authored locations. They are global pickups : once one player successfully collects an item, nobody else can collect that spawn. A full pouch shows Pouch Full and leaves it available. Starting participants Shared items 1 1–2 2 1–3 4 2–4 8 3–7 12 4–9 16 6–12 All ten cash consumables can appear, with duplicates allowed. Smoke, braces and oil are slightly less common than the original supplies; bulbs and batteries are rarer. Solo stop rolls omit the teammate-focused rescue flare. Supplies are optional: a contract never requires finding one. A pickup goes into the equipped consumable slot if empty, otherwise the first empty reserve. It is stored without being drawn. Collecting supplies awards no XP or cash. Unclaimed supplies disappear when the stop ends; collected supplies stay in your session pouch. Joins, host changes, restarts, and returning to dispatch do not reroll or replenish previously claimed supplies.

title: Dispatch FAQ
text: Dispatch FAQ Who makes SpookCo? SpookCo: Last Stop is a catnet systems production, created by kittyn , the Creator & Creative Director responsible for game design, world direction, and production. See the credits for the studio identity, development tools, and platform acknowledgments. Is this the finished game? No. SpookCo is still early in development and may change significantly after the game jam . The jam build is a working version, and its gameplay, progression, maps, and art are not final. Expect placeholder art and sound, changing balance, and unfinished edge cases. Spectator radar and AI diagnostics are development tools that may be removed. PC, Android/Quest, and iOS bundles have been built; broad device and multiplayer acceptance is still in progress. How many people can play? The implemented participant limit is 16 , and solo play is supported. Handling the creator/instance-creator overflow case of 18 people in an instance is accepted work but is not implemented yet. Do not rely on overflow admission for a playtest. Can I pass control of the game to someone else? Yes. Open Host , select a player, and offer Pass Host . They have 20 seconds to accept; the current host stays in control until acceptance. This transfers the game-host role, not VRChat’s instance ownership or master role. What if the host goes AFK? After five minutes without meaningful activity, another player can Claim Host . A visible/audible 20-second warning gives the host time to use Keep Hosting or resume meaningful input. If the host leaves, claiming becomes available immediately. Only one claim can be pending. The creator has tested Pass Host and AFK Claim Host in uploaded play. Less common cases such as claimant departure and simulation-owner suspension still need expanded testing. What else can the host do? Start ready players , Restart contract , or Cancel round / return to dispatch . Start is a click and begins the countdown; restart and cancellation retain confirmation. Restart keeps this contract’s paid claims. Cancelling preserves earnings and ends the round; the next start is a fresh contract. Ready choices persist after completion or cancellation. The host can remain unready and spectate. Why can’t I leave the van when a stop begins? For the first 10 seconds of each 20-second briefing you are kept inside the van area, so the crew reads the contract and shops together instead of scattering. A glowing line marks the edge, your status and wrist show a countdown, and Head out appears when the last 10 seconds begin. Shopping and selling at the van work the whole time. If you slip past the edge — roomscale drift, a jump from the van roof — you are placed back on your own spot after about half a second. An open shop panel survives that; a floating personal panel may still close by its own three-metre rule. Spectators, lobby players, and downed or recovering crew are never held, and the hold releases itself if anything about the round looks wrong. Why did the round start without me? Only players ready at departure join the contract. New arrivals start unready. Ready / Unready stays on until you opt out, and changes during a round apply to the next departure. See the joining rules . Why can’t I see the live field map? The map is for eligible spectators at dispatch. Joining the crew, being downed, or waiting to enter as a participant removes live tracking. A missing or delayed network snapshot displays a waiting/tracking-age message. Why does Tab stop me on desktop? That happened in the tested VRChat client, including another world. Use the direct keyboard shortcuts during movement. I can pin the menu for reading, but Tab is still needed for clicking. What makes a useful bug report? Tell the playtest organizer the platform, approximate time, number of players, area, killer, and what happened before the issue. Include whether you were host or spectator, a screenshot if useful, and the build being tested. Avoid posting raw client logs publicly; they can contain account or session details.

title: Your first shift
text: Your first shift Development build: art, balance, and features are still changing. Spectator radar and AI diagnostics are temporary development features, not promises for the finished game. Your job: finish the shared contract, get back to the van, then return to dispatch. Each round is one contract. Bring back orange cargo and fuel/repair green generators to finish both quotas. Contribute for the contract bonus; extract alive for more. Work rewards are kept if the contract fails, but that round's XP remains subject to extraction penalties. Remember three rewards: cash buys supplies for this live session; XP earns levels and perk points; commendations permanently unlock reusable gear. Survival points is the old name for commendations. Career titles and survivor field notes are longer-term goals you can explore after your first shift. 1. Get ready at dispatch Wait for saved progress to load. On your first visit, choose English or Japanese; the choice is saved and can be changed under Controls → i18n / Language . This is separate from the website's language switch. New arrivals start not ready . Click Ready / Unready to opt in. Your choice stays on between rounds until you unready; Watch / Withdraw also opts out. Your button shows your own ready status alongside the shared ready count. The game host clicks Start next round with at least one player ready. A five-second countdown appears on the ready controls. Only ready players depart; the host may remain unready and spectate. Other players can click the start control to ready/unready. Its host name follows game-host transfers, independently of VRChat master status. The office Host panel also offers Start. Find Controls & Accessibility beside the ready board. The depot's west wall has full-size field and industrial generator exhibits, diagrams for all three startup games, and a loadout poster. These are visual references, not interactive machines, and cannot consume fuel. The free practice bay is closed in this build. 2. Read the contract Each round begins with a 20-second briefing for the contract, shop and loadout. The destination and killer are rolled for each new round. The crew waits at the van for the first 10 seconds of the briefing, so there is time to shop and plan together. A glowing line marks the edge of the waiting area, and Head out appears in your status when the last 10 seconds begin and you are free to leave. Shopping and selling at the van work the whole time. 3. Head into the field The expedition lasts 150–240 seconds depending on crew size. Briarwood High School gives every crew at least seven minutes. Carry orange cargo cases back to the van and repair green equipment. Repairs retain progress when interrupted. Every required objective can be done alone without a purchased item or specific perk. At Briarwood High School , follow the hallway loop around the courtyard and use the four marked stairs to reach the basement plant. The cafeteria, gym, auditorium, library and basement stay open at every crew size. Classrooms open in groups: 9 for 1–2 players, 18 for 3–4, 27 for 5–7, and all 36 for 8 or more. Check the ground/B1 tabs on the van map. Generators start dry. Small field generators need one can; industrial diesel generators need two. Find cans around the unlocked map and carry them against the machine: each can stays attached. Industrial controls unlock only after both cans arrive. Every round spawns two or three spare cans beyond its actual requirement. Solo and duo rounds use one small generator. Crews of 3–8 get at least one of each size; 9–12 get at least two small and one industrial; 13–16 get at least two of each. Remaining choices and their positions are randomized when the round starts. A short pole marks the machine's state: slow flashing red means empty, solid red means one of two cans, orange means startup required, and pale green means running. Minigame panels have a translucent backing so movement behind them stays visible. Use the controls on the front to complete one shuffled startup task: Prime and purge: pump until the fuel chamber fills, then bleed the trapped air. Clear three pockets and press Start Engine. Extra pumping and early bleeding make noise. Listen and tune: adjust choke and throttle until both read Steady, then press Start Engine. The sound and visual meters give the same information. Route the fuel: turn three valves to connect the top-left supply to the bottom-right engine inlet, then press Start Engine. More than one route works. The first three fueled generators draw all three games in a random order. A task stays assigned and keeps its progress when you step away. One person operates a generator at a time; someone else can take over after they leave or stop working. Mistakes attract the hunter from farther away. Mechanic and tool oil make the controls more forgiving, and repair tape fixes one task step without skipping the final start. Finishing a generator also powers nearby active gear: stay within six metres with no solid wall between you and the machine to recharge twice as fast . It keeps working during extraction. The machine label and your HUD/wrist show the benefit; killers can still reach you there. Crew at stop start Cargo Repairs 1 2 1 2 3 1 3–4 5 2 5–8 8 3 9–12 12 4 13–16 16 5 Players joining the world wait for the next round and do not raise the active quota. Departures and withdrawals can lower requirements while preserving finished work. Downed players and teammates sheltering at the van still count. The field is not the same twice. Every stop rolls fresh obstacles — hay bales, broken-down vehicles, fallen trees, crates and drums — alongside the usual random supplies, and worksite front doors can be opened and closed while you work. See know the threats for how the hunter deals with a door you shut behind you. 4. Regroup and extract The covered campfire refuge beside the van is protected throughout the stop. Enter and leave freely. The current van body is a solid placeholder; use the covered exterior, not the van’s body as an entrance. Finishing the quota starts extraction early, with 60–90 seconds depending on the crew-size tier, or at least 90 seconds at Briarwood . Running out of expedition time triggers emergency extraction instead. Get back before departure: it does not wait indefinitely for missing players. Transit takes 10 seconds : the view fades to black over one second and stays dark with a short next-stop message while walking pauses, then fades in at the next van. Standing avatars are never driven around. Menus cannot be opened during transit. The crew arrives spread around the van on separate spots rather than stacked on one point, and the same applies whenever the game moves you — a restart, a recovery, or returning to dispatch. After a completed contract, gold-strapped BONUS SALVAGE cases become available near the van's surrounding work area: one for an initial crew of 1–2, two for 3–8, or three for 9–16. Bring them back using the normal cargo controls. Each pays double normal cargo XP and $24 , and a real handoff shares credit. They are optional and never raise the required quota. The extraction clock keeps running. The crew gets an eight-second decision window before the usual all-aboard departure check starts; everyone can stay aboard and skip the salvage. Unfinished bonus cases never hold the van past its deadline. Failed contracts unlock no bonus work, and restarting a stop never replenishes a bonus case that already paid. Missing extraction keeps only 10% of your round XP. Each dispatched player left behind also reduces everyone's round XP by 10%, capped at 50%; previous rounds' XP stays untouched. One completed contract finishes the round. A short result shows the outcome and your cash, XP and commendations, then everyone returns to dispatch. Staying safe without contributing does not earn the contract bonus. Players who remain ready join the next round when the host starts it. Lethal attacks Roadkill's charge, warned catches from Hitchhiker and Usher, and gunshots from Warden and Deadeye eliminate you for the rest of the round, even with Hardhat or Second Wind. You drop what you are carrying and can spectate at dispatch. If everyone is eliminated, the stop ends promptly. Your banked rewards remain. See killer counterplay for warnings and escape routes. If you go down You normally start with two health. A short immunity interval prevents immediate repeated hits. Going down puts you on the floor: you crawl slowly, you cannot jump, and you drop whatever you were carrying. Your first down of a stop gives you 20 seconds ; every later down in the same stop gives you 10. Getting someone up is a hold. One rescuer takes 10 seconds , and every extra pair of hands takes a quarter off that — 7.5 seconds for two, 5.6 for three. Field Medic halves whatever the crew's time is. While anyone is holding the revive your countdown stops; if they let go, half of the time they put in is added back to your clock, so a partial revive still buys you something. If no able teammate remains, including solo play, your countdown is cut to a few seconds rather than run in full — nothing can answer it, but you still get that long on the floor. Otherwise, when your countdown expires, what happens depends on when you went down. In the first half of a stop an eight-second recovery returns you to the van. After halfway you are out for the rest of that stop: you return to dispatch, can watch the live field map, and join the next host-started round if you remain ready. Dropped cargo can be recovered either way. Capture never removes banked XP or commendations. Second Wind allows a six-second field recovery on the first ordinary down of a stop; it cannot revive an elimination. Joining a round already in progress New arrivals stay at dispatch and start unready. Ready / Unready during a round sets your choice for the next departure; it does not join or withdraw you from the active contract. Unreadying in the field lets you finish this round and sit out the next. Your ready choice lasts until you change it or leave the instance. Continue with controls , equipment , and killer counterplay .

title: Progression & saving
text: Progression & saving The save system is implemented, but reconnect and multi-instance edge cases still need expanded uploaded testing. Do not treat a development build as a permanent economy guarantee. What stays with you Resource Purpose Intended lifetime XP Levels and perk-point capacity Permanent across visits Commendations Lifetime equipment milestones; never spent Permanent across visits Career mastery Job and killer ranks; cosmetic crew titles Permanent across visits Cash Buy consumables The live instance session Consumable pouch Purchased and scavenged supplies The live instance session Build and controls Perk/equipment choices and device preferences Saved across visits Rejoining the same live session is designed to restore cash, pouch contents, and relevant equipment state. A → B → A uses separate records while A remains live. Up to 128 recent sessions are retained. When everyone leaves, that session ends; a later fresh session begins with fresh cash and supplies. Wait for restoration before shopping or collecting. Accepted changes are saved during play, not just on departure. A sudden crash can lose the most recent cloud write. Capture does not remove banked XP or commendations. Earn your contract bonus Moving around or waiting in the van does not count as work. Contribute by delivering cargo, bringing fuel to a generator, completing or meaningfully helping a repair, rescuing a teammate, or using gear to interrupt an active chase or warning. Result XP Cash Commendations A contract your crew completes and you contributed to 25 10 1 You also extract alive from that completed contract 15 5 1 more Failed contract, even if you reach the van No round bonus No round bonus 0 You did not contribute No round bonus No round bonus 0 Round XP is provisional until extraction. Failing to extract keeps only 10% of your earned round XP. Every dispatched player who fails to extract also reduces everyone's round XP by 10%, capped at 50%. Apply the personal reduction first, then the crew reduction, and round the final total down. A player who misses extraction with one crew member missing keeps 9%; with five or more missing, they keep 5%. A player who extracts with two missing keeps 80%. Only the current round's XP is reduced. Previously banked XP, cash and commendations are untouched. The dispatched roster includes disconnected players; spectators and later arrivals do not add penalties. A failed contract provides no contract or extraction bonus. If you contributed and the crew completes the contract after you are eliminated, its XP bonus is included in the reduced total. Cancelling a live contract settles it as a failed extraction. Cargo and repair finishers earn 10 / 12 / 20 / 30 XP for an initial crew of 1–2 / 3–4 / 5–8 / 9+ respectively. Cargo pays $8, repair pays $12, and fully fueling a generator pays $4 with the same crew-scaled XP. A player who supplies the first can to a two-can generator receives helper credit when a teammate supplies the second. Scrapper increases objective cash by 20%. Optional bonus salvage unlocks only after the required contract is complete. Its finisher earns 20 / 24 / 40 / 60 XP for the same initial-crew brackets and $24 per case. Qualified handoff helpers receive half; Scrapper applies normally. Cash is awarded on delivery; the XP remains subject to extraction penalties. There are only one to three bonus cases per stop, and each pays once per trip, including restarts. A cargo helper must carry the case at least three metres before handing it off. A repair helper must supply at least 10% of the completed repair. Qualified helpers receive half the objective XP and cash when someone finishes the task. Picking up and dropping a case or tapping a generator is not enough. Restarting a stop does not pay the same objective again. Rescue credit is bounded to 10 XP / $3 per rescuer per stop. Gear that successfully interrupts an active threat can grant 8 XP / $3 once per stop; repeatedly distracting an idle killer grants nothing. Each round ends after one contract. There is no additional three-stop shift payout. Contribute to a completed contract and extract alive to earn 40 base XP, $15 and 2 commendations , on top of your completed work rewards. The XP total still receives any crew extraction penalty. The result screen shows your outcome, total cash, XP and commendations, then the return-to-dispatch countdown. Each reward line explains its use. The menu keeps the work, contract and extraction breakdown and next equipment unlock. Commendations is the current name for survival points; existing balances retain their value and are never spent. Career mastery and titles Open Perks , advance past Specialist perks, then choose Career mastery . Two career pages show your counts, next rank and title choices. Select an earned title to display it beside your name in the crew roster, or choose No title to hide it. Titles automatically show your current rank, I, II or III. They are cosmetic and give no combat advantage. Track What counts Rank I / II / III Hauler Paid cargo deliveries, including bonus salvage and qualified handoff assists 5 / 25 / 100 Engineer Paid generator fuel and completed repairs, including qualified repair assists 5 / 25 / 100 Crew Support Paid rescues and useful gear support; each category counts once per stop 5 / 25 / 100 Each of the ten killers Contribute to a completed contract and extract alive from that killer 3 / 10 / 25 Finishing work and meaningfully helping earn equal mastery credit, even though helper XP and cash are smaller. Merely surviving, failing the contract or missing extraction gives no killer mastery. Restarting the same stop cannot repeat its paid mastery. Job progress already earned survives a failed stop. Older records that remember surviving a killer begin with one proven escape for that killer. They cannot reconstruct old job counts. Mastery and title selection save with your permanent profile. Levels and perk points Start at level 1 with 2 points . Gain a point at levels 2, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 28, 32, 36 and 40 , reaching 15 points at level 40 . The early gains let you afford a four-point perk at level 3. Choose any combination of unique perks within your budget and respec freely during briefings. Perk Cost Current effect Spotter 1 Objective markers visible 50% farther away Courier 2 Removes the cargo movement penalty Mechanic 2 Stronger primer strokes, forgiving engine tuning, and a highlighted break in the fuel route Field Medic 2 Halves the required revive time Scrapper 2 20% more objective cash Soft Soles 3 Movement hearing range reduced by 25% Adrenaline 3 Extraction movement bonus Quickdraw 3 Active equipment cooldowns reduced by 20% Hardhat 4 One extra maximum health; does not protect against lethal attacks Second Wind 4 Six-second field recovery on first ordinary down each stop; cannot reverse elimination Silent Tools 2 Level 3: halves repair noise range; footsteps are unchanged Ear Defenders 2 Level 3: halves howl slow duration; does not affect fog Escape Artist 4 Level 10: partial peeks take longer to confirm and visual searches last 35% less time; hearing still matters Braced 3 Level 6: 15% faster sideways movement for dodging; no lethal-hit immunity Clear Lenses 2 Level 6: reduces hazard fog density by 35%; ordinary world fog remains Sixth Sense 3 Level 9: HUD warning when a nearby killer winds up an attack, within 25 m Trailbreaker 3 Level 12: searches based on your footsteps last 35% less time; sight is unchanged Inspector 2 Level 3: identifies the nearest visible, unclaimed field supply within 8 m The two-page perk menu shows cost, required level and equipped state. The original ten perks have no extra level requirement. Saved affordable builds keep their selections. Combined general movement bonuses are capped at 20%; Braced separately improves sideways movement by 15%. Perks support different roles; required tasks remain possible with the starter loadout. XP comes from completed work, bounded rescue/support credit, contributed contract and extraction results. Idle waiting, movement alone, and supply collection do not generate XP. The early level curve stays unchanged through level 10. Each subsequent level costs the base amount ( 150 + 35 × (current level − 1) ) multiplied by the current band: Current level XP cost multiplier 1–9 1× 10–14 2× 15–19 5× 20–24 12× 25–29 16× 30–34 20× 35–39 24× Level 10 requires 2,610 banked XP, level 15 7,960 , level 20 25,710 , and level 40 456,310 . Perk-point milestones stay spaced across those levels; the budget still caps at 15. Later permanent equipment requires both a level and commendation milestone. Actual days or hours to reach these milestones depend on contributions and extraction success and need live balance data.

title: Know the threats
text: Know the threats One killer is active at a time. Melee hunters keep pace with a running employee and gain speed with larger crews. Warden and Deadeye move more slowly, but threaten firing lanes at a distance. Read the warning and use each killer's recovery window. Killer What it does What to try Groundskeeper Sight pursuit, remembered routes, and local searches Break sight, change route, and quietly leave its search area. Rattletrap Blind; investigates movement and task noise Walk when possible, time repairs, and use a decoy. Roadkill Telegraphs a lethal, committed charge Dodge sideways and put solid cover between you and its line. Hitchhiker Ambushes from concealed positions; warned catches are lethal Watch roadside silhouettes and change approach. Usher Warns before a lethal chase from its vision cone Get out of the cone or behind cover before the lock completes. Switchboard Pursues and marks work-site/route hazards Leave the marked area and switch sites. Hound Follows aging movement trails as well as sight Creep, double back, and leave the old trail behind. Trailbreaker helps. Mimic Disguises itself as false cargo, then warns before revealing Watch for eyes, twitching and creaks. Back away; Inspector can identify it. Warden Warns, commits to a shotgun fan, fires, then reloads Leave the fan or reach solid cover. Move while it reloads. Deadeye Confirms sight, warns with a rifle line, commits and fires Break sight before the red lock or sidestep afterward. It changes position between shots. Your footsteps matter Creeping is quiet for ordinary killers. Footsteps grow louder gradually as you move faster, and solid cover greatly reduces their reach. Rattletrap is the hearing specialist: it can detect slower movement and hear more through cover. Running is much riskier than walking. Soft Soles reduces movement hearing ranges by 25%. A brief head-only or body-only peek builds suspicion before a sighted killer confirms you. Repeated peeks accumulate suspicion, and showing both your head and torso confirms you immediately. Once a killer is tracking you, a currently visible head or torso is enough to maintain a recent chase. Full cover still breaks sight, and cover does not erase a route the killer already saw. This senses in-game movement and certain task events. It does not listen to microphone audio or voice chat. Hiding in shrubs Dense shrubs conceal you from ordinary monster vision and reduce your walking, running and sideways movement speed by 50% while your body is inside. Leaving restores your normal speed. The slowdown stacks with carried cargo, perks and temporary effects. Break sight before entering. A monster actively chasing or aiming at you can keep tracking you if it watches you enter. If you break its view, it can still search the last place it saw you, but cannot simply reacquire you through the shrub. Standing on top of foliage does not count as hiding. Bushes do not suppress hearing, erase Hound trails, stop committed bullets or charges, or make you invulnerable. Rattletrap remains a hearing specialist. Quiet movement and a route change still matter. Cars, trailers, equipment and wooden fences provide solid cover. Chain-link fencing blocks passage while allowing sight through it; plan around its openings. One corner is not a guaranteed escape Hunters can continue toward the last observed route, investigate sound, scan while moving, and check nearby paths. They pursue fresh evidence promptly, then search more carefully. Search budgets vary by killer: running out of nearby routes does not instantly erase their memory, and a temporarily blocked path can lead to a local search. Warden and Deadeye also search beyond simply reaching your last known position. Quietly escaping still works; without fresh evidence every search ends. Escape Artist shortens visual searches; Trailbreaker shortens sound searches and makes Hound trails fade sooner. Break sight, change route, reduce noise, and use the protected refuge when needed. Sound gives the AI an investigation point; it is not treated as direct vision through a wall. Running in a straight line is unreliable against melee hunters. They lead their turns instead of trailing you, and inside about three metres they can lunge. A landed hit costs them a moment's recovery, which is the gap you use to reach cover, a door or the van. Carrying a case slows you below their pace: drop it if you are being run down. Lethal attacks Roadkill's charge, a warned catch from Hitchhiker or Usher, and a hit from Warden or Deadeye eliminate you for the rest of the round. Hardhat and Second Wind cannot save you from these attacks. Spawn and rescue immunity still protect you. Hitchhiker and Usher must warn before committing; breaking sight cancels their lethal chase, and a missed commitment gives you a recovery window. Solid cover stops contact through walls. You can spectate from dispatch, and you join the next host-started round if you remain ready. If the whole crew is eliminated, the stop ends promptly. Eliminated players do not reduce the required task quota, and reconnecting or toggling readiness does not undo elimination. Reading a gun warning Amber aim follows you during the warning. Red aim is committed to a fixed line or fan: a late sidestep can avoid it. Solid cover blocks the actual shot, including after commitment. Smoke can break acquisition or an uncommitted aim, but it cannot stop a bullet already aimed at your position. Decoys redirect an uncommitted gun killer; they cannot cancel its warning once aiming starts. A successful flash or trip alarm interrupts it and makes it confirm you again. Warden must reload after its shotgun blast. Deadeye reloads and looks for a new firing position. Neither deals melee contact damage. False cargo and old trails Mimic cargo is separate from real objectives. It never takes away delivered work. Its breathing, eyes and twitch are clues before the reveal; Inspector identifies a nearby visible disguise. Smoke can conceal your approach, and the reveal warning gives you time to back away. The Hound follows recorded movement only after a delay. Quiet creeping leaves no new trail; old samples expire instead of tracking your hidden position. It can still see you normally, so use cover as you leave the trail. Doors, and a field that changes every stop Worksite front doors can be opened and closed. Shut one behind you and the hunter has to deal with it: an unhurried one opens it, but a hunter that is chasing you breaks it off its hinge , and a broken door cannot be closed again. A door buys you distance once, so spend it well. Nobody can close a door on a person standing in the doorway, and the rear opening of every worksite stays clear so you are never sealed in. The field itself is rolled again at the start of every stop: hay bales, broken-down vehicles, fallen trees, crates, oil drums and more appear in different places, alongside the usual random supplies. Learn the landmarks, not the route. Spectating the current build Choose Watch / Withdraw to remain at dispatch. The Live Field Map shows crew and killer tracking. In the current test build, a gold outline depicts vision and blue rings depict walking/running hearing; Rattletrap has hearing only. Tracking is for lobby spectators, not active or downed crew. Development feature: visible sensing radar and AI diagnostics may change or disappear from the final game. The map is a simplified horizontal view, not a guarantee of detection at every height or through every shape of cover.

title: SpookCo: Last Stop
text: The night shift has a survival clause. Take the company van into the dark. Recover cargo, patch up the equipment, and get everyone back to the campfire lantern before departure. Something out there heard you clock in. One contract. Get the crew home. SpookCo: Last Stop is a cooperative horror world built around short expeditions and a dependable refuge. Play alone or bring a crew of up to 16. Finish the work, scavenge what you can, and decide when to make a run for the van. Clock in Ready up at dispatch, choose your equipment, and read the contract. Stay ready for future rounds; the host starts each departure. Do the work Recover cargo and repair equipment. Field supplies are shared: whoever collects a pickup gets it. Running is faster, but it carries farther through the dark. Make it back The van’s covered campfire refuge stays safe. Complete the quota to open extraction early, or scramble aboard during emergency extraction. Departure has a deadline. A small world with a long night ahead Contracts use the authored destinations: Camp Deadwood , Last Chance Service Station , Calder laboratory , and Briarwood High School . Ten killers use different senses and attack patterns. Some follow movement noise or old trails; others disguise themselves or warn before a lethal charge, catch, or gunshot. Quiet movement, cover, doors and knowing when to move matter. Required work earns rewards and opens extraction. Once the contract is complete, optional bonus salvage offers more XP and cash within the existing departure deadline. Repaired generators recharge nearby active gear faster. Eighteen perks, ten consumables, five reusable tools and persistent job/killer mastery provide choices across shifts; standing around to survive does not earn a round bonus. This is a playable build still early in development , and it may change significantly after the game jam . Gameplay, progression, maps, and art are all subject to change. The local expansion includes dressed maps, darker dispatch lighting, distance fog and a glowing lounge CRT. Balance, device performance and multiplayer edge cases still need playtesting. Spectator sensing radar and AI diagnostics remain development tools and may change before release. Your first shift Start with the quick-start guide , check your controls , or learn what to pack in the equipment guide . The site describes the current baseline; an older uploaded build may behave differently. A catnet systems production, created by kittyn . Meet the creator and view the credits →
